segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Hello, and thank you for asking me to your teachers' meeting to talk about the Dinosaur Museum and to tell you a bit about what you can do with your students there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, let me give you some of the basic informationfirst.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In regard to opening hours, we're open every day of the week from 9.00 am to 8.00 pm except on Mondays when we close at 1.30 pm.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And, in fact the only day in the year when we're closed is on the 25th of & 12 December.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You can book a guided tour for your school group any time that we're open.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you bring a school group to the museum,when you arrive we ask you to remain with your group in the car park.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: One or more of the tour guides will welcome you there and brief you about what the tour will be about.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We do this there because our entrance is quite small and we really haven't got much room for briefing groups in the exhibition area.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As far as the amount of time you'll need goes, if you bring a school group you should plan on allowing a minimum of 90 minutes for the visit.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This allows 15 minutes to get on and off the coach, 45 minutes for the guided tour and 30 minutes for after-tour activities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you're going to have lunch at the museum you will, of course, have to allow more time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are two cafes in the museum,with seating for 80 people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you want to eat there you'll need to reserve some seating, as they can get quite crowded at lunch time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then outside the museum at the back there are tables, and students can bring their own lunch and eat it there in the open air.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When the students come into the museumfoyer we ask them to check in their backpacks with their books, lunch boxes, etc, at the cloakroom before they enter the museum proper.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I'm afraid in the past we have had a few things gon·emissing after school visits so this is a strict rule.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Also, some of the exhibits are fragile and we don't want them to be accidentally knocked.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But we do provide school studentswith handoutswith questions and quizzes on -18 them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There's so much that students_can learn in the museum and it's fun for them to have something to do.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Of course they'll need to bring somethingto write with for these.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We do -18 allow students to take photographs.For students who are doing projects it's useful to make some kind of visual record of what they see that they can add to their reports.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And finally, they should not bring anything to eat into the museum, or drinks of any kind.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are also a few things the students can do after the tour.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the theatrette on the ground 'floorthere are continuousscreeningsof short documentariesabout dinosaurs 019 & 20 which they can see at any time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We used to have an activity room with more interactive things like making models of dinosaurs and drawing and painting pictures,even hunting for dinosaur eggs, but unfortunatelythe room was damagedin a bad storm recentlywhen water came in the roof, so that's closed at the moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But we do have an IT centre where students have access to CD ROMs with a range of dinosaurgames.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: These games are a lot 019 & 20 of fun, but they also teach the students about the lives of dinosaurs,how they found food, protectedtheir habitat, survived threats, that kind of thing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And ...

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I think that's all I have to tell you.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Pleasefeel free to ask any questions if you would like to know anything else ...
